messages:
maya: Quick check-in — I compared on-demand layerwise hydration vs microchunk streaming for large safetensors. Initial result: layerwise wins for PCIe-bound hosts, microchunks win for high-loss networks.
tony: Interesting. What about wasted decrypts with microchunks?
li: Microchunks have more metadata overhead but let us abort early on bad ranges. We saw ~12% extra IO but 70% fewer wasted decrypts on flaky links.
kevin: Layerwise is simpler for GPU slab allocation though. We can keep contiguous slabs and avoid fragmentation.
maya: Agreed. Also easier to implement zeroing guarantees per-layer. Microchunks need a micro-assembler to coalesce into slabs.
tony: Proposal: default to layerwise + microchunk fallback when network QoS low or when proof-fail rates > threshold. Also add a runtime flag for customers who prefer maximum IO predictability.
li: Add metrics before rollout: microchunk_proof_fail_rate, wasted_decrypts, slab_fragmentation_pct.
kevin: For KMS: keep token-header mode for hosted, per-layer KMS for enterprise. No per-microchunk KMS.
maya: Next actions: I’ll write a short spec that lists header formats for both modes and an ops playbook for fallback.
warmup-bot: warmup-bot: trial run wnp-2111 model=redwood-m-65b mode=layerwise+microchunk-fallback peak_decrypted_mb=96 wasted_prefetch_mb=2 proof_fail_count=1
